title: Rocks and the Rock Cycle
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Rocks and the Rock Cycle Worksheets (Igneous, Sedimentary, Metamorphic)
standard_text: The composition of the Earth; the structure of the Earth; the rock cycle and the formation of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks; Earth as a source of limited resources and the efficacy of recycling.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on rocks: the structure of the Earth, igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks, crystal size, weathering, erosion and the rock cycle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rocks change from one type to another.
key_sub: Igneous from magma, sedimentary from layers, metamorphic from heat and pressure.
body_html:
How to think about it

There are three types of rock, and the rock cycle links them.

  • Igneous: magma or lava cools. Slow cooling gives large crystals; fast cooling gives small ones.
  • Sedimentary: weathering, erosion, deposition, compaction and cementation. Porous, often with fossils.
  • Metamorphic: heat and pressure change rock without melting (limestone → marble).
Example

Basalt: large or small crystals?

Lava cooled quickly

Answer: small

Example

Water freezes in a crack. Type of weathering?

Ice expands

Answer: freeze-thaw

Common mistakes

  • Thinking metamorphic rock forms by melting.
  • Mixing up weathering and erosion.
  • Thinking the mantle is a liquid.

faq.q: What are the three types of rock?
faq.a: Igneous (formed when magma or lava cools), sedimentary (formed from layers of sediment) and metamorphic (formed when rock is changed by heat and pressure).

faq.q: Why do some igneous rocks have large crystals?
faq.a: Magma that cools slowly deep underground gives crystals time to grow. Lava that cools quickly on the surface forms small crystals.

faq.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
faq.a: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces where it is. Erosion moves the pieces away, for example in rivers or by wind.
